post.summary: Submit a job to OpenVibe.Run: POST /api/v1/jobs.
post.description: **run.job.submit** (public): Submit a job to OpenVibe.Run: POST /api/v1/jobs. The job belongs to the token's project, which is billed per wall-clock second it runs (service run, operation function.invoke, unit s). An idempotency_key makes a retry return the first job.

get.summary: Read one of the token project's jobs: GET /api/v1/jobs/:id (state, placement, timings, exit, usage seconds, result).
get.description: **run.job.read** (public): Read one of the token project's jobs: GET /api/v1/jobs/:id (state, placement, timings, exit, usage seconds, result).

post.summary: Cancel one of the token project's jobs: POST /api/v1/jobs/:id/cancel.
post.description: **run.job.cancel** (public): Cancel one of the token project's jobs: POST /api/v1/jobs/:id/cancel. A queued or placed job never starts; a running one is killed (platform.job-frame@1 job_cancel); cancelling an ended job changes nothing and answers it as it is.

get.description: **run.session.read** (public): Read your own browser sessions: GET /api/v1/sessions (run.session-list-result@1) and GET /api/v1/sessions/:id (run.session@1: state, where it runs, timings, desk-seconds). Never another person's.

post.summary: Open a browser session for yourself (the Desks plan's D6): POST /api/v1/sessions with run.session-create-request@1.
post.description: **run.session.create** (public): Open a browser session for yourself (the Desks plan's D6): POST /api/v1/sessions with run.session-create-request@1. Run places a browser desk on one of your own machines (when you name it or your requirements name user-owned) or on a desk host that serves other people, where every desk runs in its own sandbox, and answers run.session@1. A first-party service acting for a person (X-OV-Subject) opens it for them and is recorded as via. Desk time is metered in desk-seconds.

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

identity.subject-ref.v1.title: SubjectRef
identity.subject-ref.v1.description: The one cross-platform reference to an actor. Issued by OpenVibe.Network. Never a service-local integer id.

oneOf.description: AgentSubject: an agent (OpenVibe.Actor, or a developer app's agent) acting under grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2). In an event envelope, on_behalf_of names the owner.

platform.runtime-class.v1.title: RuntimeClass
platform.runtime-class.v1.description: platform.runtime-class@1: the kind of execution environment a platform.job@1 asks for (plan T14 Run; ADR-034 proposed). A name only: this contract defines no behavior, and a worker runs only the classes it advertises and refuses every other one (`nack`). `function` is the first class implemented (OpenVibe.Node's function worker); the others are reserved names. Each class names one reserved Fabric capability in platform.resource-offer@1.capabilities — `worker:` + the class (worker:function, worker:code, worker:browser, worker:linux, worker:desktop, worker:gpu) — and a node advertises the name of each class it runs.
platform.runtime-class.v1.$comment: Additive: a class may be added to v1; none is removed, renamed or reordered.

oneOf.description: A pre-registered artifact (name and exact version) run once with declared args to one result: single-shot, no persistent filesystem, no dependency resolution, network denied.
Arbitrary source with its dependency tree in a longer-lived environment; needs image handling and isolation stronger than a container.
A headless or headed web browser session driven remotely.
A full Linux environment (shell, filesystem, processes) that lives across commands.
A graphical desktop session with screen and input under control levels.
A workload that holds one or more GPUs for its lifetime.

platform.workload-requirements.v1.title: WorkloadRequirements
platform.workload-requirements.v1.description: What a workload needs, so the platform can place it (roadmap WS-Z9). Hard constraints are filtered before any objective is scored; a cheaper candidate that misses one is never chosen.

kind.description: what runs, e.g. watch.browser, media.transcode, ai.run, events.deliver

residency.description: region or jurisdiction the work and its data must stay in

trust.description: trust classes allowed to run it (ADR-046); when absent, first-party, partner, community and external. user-owned is never a default: a user-owned offer is eligible only when this list names it

partition_key.description: stable key for rendezvous placement (room, stream, session)

run.job-create-request.v1.title: RunJobCreateRequest
run.job-create-request.v1.description: run.job-create-request@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1, ADR-034): the body of POST /api/v1/jobs on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.job.submit). The job belongs to the project the caller's token names, or, for a first-party service acting for a person (X-OV-Subject), the project it names with X-OV-Project once Network confirms the person is an admin or owner of it (ADR-003 amendment 2026-10-12); the person is then the requester and the service is recorded as via. CLASS is a platform.runtime-class@1 name; Run accepts any of them but places a job only on a node that advertises worker:<class> (platform.resource-offer@1), so a class no node runs today (browser, linux, desktop, gpu) ends expired with run.job.unplaceable. ARTIFACT is the pre-registered artifact to run (name and one exact version), required for function and code, as platform.job@1 carries it. ARGS is the artifact's declared input as JSON (at most 512 KiB serialized, else 413). INPUTS are files placed in the job directory before the process starts, each an OpenVibe.Media object pinned by its sha256: a size or digest mismatch fails the job (run.job.input_digest_mismatch) before the process ever runs; Run never fetches a caller-chosen URL. LIMITS are hard caps merged stricter with the node's own (platform.job@1 limits); a request over the project's tier cap is refused 422 run.limits.exceeded, never silently lowered. EGRESS is the network the job may reach, the values of OpenVibe.Node's worker.egress, carried per job as the same-named platform.job@1 net: none (default; no network), public or openvibe-only. A job asking for public or openvibe-only is placed only on a node whose worker.egress allows it; a worker whose host policy is stricter runs the stricter one. REQUIREMENTS (platform.workload-requirements@1) narrow placement; absent means { kind: run.<class>, mobility: job, latency_class: background, objective: balanced }. IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: a repeat from the same project within 24 h with an identical body answers the first job (200, created false); with a different body 409 run.idempotency.conflict. NODE pins the machine: the device id (dev_…) of the job's own machine in Run's placement (platform.resource-offer@1 node_id, as GET /api/v1/machines on OpenVibe.Bot names it), answered by 409 run.job.node_offline when that machine is not connected, never moved to another one (Codes C9c).

args.description: The artifact's declared input as JSON; default {}.

inputs.description: Files placed in the job directory before the process starts; names are unique (else 422).

ttl_ms.description: Lifetime from creation, covering the wait for a node and the run (platform.job@1 ttl_ms); when it runs out the job ends expired. Default: limits.wall_ms plus 600000.

node.description: The machine to run on, pinned: the device id (dev_…) of the job's own machine in Run's placement, as platform.resource-offer@1 node_id and OpenVibe.Bot's GET /api/v1/machines name it (Codes C9c). Run places the job only on that machine and refuses it 409 run.job.node_offline when it is not connected, never moving it to another one. Absent: Run places it on any machine that fits.

artifact.description: The pre-registered artifact to run (platform.job@1 artifact).

version.description: One exact version, never a range

input.description: One input file: an OpenVibe.Media object the caller's project can read, pinned by digest.

name.description: File name in the job directory; no path separators.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the object's bytes.

limits.description: Caps on the running process (platform.job@1 limits); hitting one ends the job failed with run.job.limit.

egress.description: OpenVibe.Node worker.egress values: none (no network), public (the internet without private, link-local or the network's own ranges), openvibe-only (the network's own endpoints only).

run.job-create-result.v1.title: RunJobCreateResult
run.job-create-result.v1.description: run.job-create-result@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1, ADR-034): the answer of POST /api/v1/jobs on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.job.submit). 201 with created true and the new job, queued; 200 with created false and the job first created under the same idempotency_key (in whatever state it has reached). Refusals are application/problem+json: 400 (body invalid), 413 (args over 512 KiB), 422 run.limits.exceeded or a duplicate input name, 409 run.idempotency.conflict, 429 (quota).

created.description: false when the idempotency_key matched an earlier job.

run.job-list-query.v1.title: RunJobListQuery
run.job-list-query.v1.description: run.job-list-query@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1): the query string of GET /api/v1/jobs on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.job.list) and of GET /api/v1/admin/jobs (run.job.admin, which alone may pass project_id). Without project_id it lists the caller's token project.

project_id.description: Admin only (run.job.admin): list this project's jobs; with run.job.list it is refused 403.

limit.description: Items per page, 1 to 200 (default 50). A query string carries it as a string, which must name the same range.

run.job-list-result.v1.title: RunJobListResult
run.job-list-result.v1.description: run.job-list-result@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1): the answer of GET /api/v1/jobs on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.job.list) and GET /api/v1/admin/jobs (run.job.admin), filtered by run.job-list-query@1. Jobs come newest first (by id). More fields may be added.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; null on the last page.

run.job-read-result.v1.title: RunJobReadResult
run.job-read-result.v1.description: run.job-read-result@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1, ADR-034): one job on OpenVibe.Run, as GET /api/v1/jobs/{id} answers it (capability run.job.read), POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel answers it after the cancel (run.job.cancel), and run.job-create-result@1 and run.job-list-result@1 carry it. STATES: queued (stored, waiting for a node) -> placed (sent to a node as platform.job@1, not yet started) -> running (the node sent job_started) -> one end state: succeeded (job_exit reason exited with code 0), failed (exited with another code, or reason limit, stopped or failed), cancelled (POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel, or job_exit reason cancelled), expired (ttl_ms ran out: before placement, before start, or while running, job_exit reason ttl). An end state never changes. Run mints the id (job_<ULID>) and sends it unchanged as platform.job@1 `id`, so every metering reading of the job is `run:<id>:<n>` (platform.job-frame@1 job_usage). usage.seconds is wall_ms / 1000: the sum of the job's readings (service run, operation function.invoke, unit s). Never carries the job's stdout (GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/stream) or a credential. More fields may be added.

id.description: Minted by Run; the platform.job@1 id and the stem of every usage reading key (run:<id>:<n>).

project_id.description: The project the caller's token names; usage is billed to it.

requester.description: The token principal that submitted the job.

ttl_ms.description: The job's lifetime from created_at, the default filled in.

requirements.description: What the job was placed against, the default filled in.

placement.description: Where the job was sent; null while queued, and for a job cancelled or expired before placement.

started_at.description: From job_started started_ms; null until the process started.

finished_at.description: When the job reached its end state; null before.

exit.description: The node's job_exit; null until it arrived, and for a job that ended before a node ran it.

result.description: The artifact's declared output (job_exit result, any JSON); null unless state is succeeded.

error.description: Why the job failed or expired; null in every other state.

node.description: The worker's device id (the usage reading's `node`).

provider.description: The offer's provider (the usage reading's `provider`); null for a first-party node.

code.description: The process's exit status; null when it was killed or never ran.

seconds.description: Metered wall-clock seconds, wall_ms / 1000 (unit s); 0 when the job never started.

code.description: run.job.exit_nonzero, run.job.limit, run.job.stopped, run.job.worker_failed, run.job.input_digest_mismatch, run.job.unplaceable (expired: no node offered the class, egress and requirements), run.job.ttl.

run.job-stream-ticket-result.v1.title: RunJobStreamTicketResult
run.job-stream-ticket-result.v1.description: run.job-stream-ticket-result@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1): the answer of POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/stream/ticket on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.job.stream), modelled on Events' realtime ticket (network.realtime-ticket-result@1). A browser cannot put a header on an EventSource, so it opens `${stream_url}?ticket=${ticket}` (plus Last-Event-ID when it resumes) at once. The ticket is a two-minute RS256 JWT that Run signs: audience openvibe.run, typ run-stream (so it is never a session token), it names this one job, and Run refuses a jti it has already seen while the ticket is valid, so a ticket opens one stream; ask for a fresh one for every reconnect. Never logged, never stored. A server caller may instead send its Bearer token to GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/stream. The stream is text/event-stream of run.job-stream-event@1.

run.session-control-request.v1.title: RunSessionControlRequest
run.session-control-request.v1.description: run.session-control-request@1 (the Desks plan's D6): one command on a session's desk, the body of POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/commands on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.session.control), answered with run.session-control-result@1. KIND and VALUE are bot.command@1's for that kind (screen: a picture of the page; input: the mouse, wheel and keys on the page; browser: open, click, fill, press, back, read, screenshot) without desk, which is always the session's own: Run carries the command to OpenVibe.Bot on the session's lease (bot.desk-lease@1) and nothing on the machine other than that desk is reachable. A command on a session that is not running is refused 409 run.session.not_running. ID makes a retry safe: the same id within the session answers the first result.

value.description: bot.command@1's value for that kind, without desk (refused 422 if it names another desk).

run.session-control-result.v1.title: RunSessionControlResult
run.session-control-result.v1.description: run.session-control-result@1 (the Desks plan's D6): the answer to run.session-control-request@1. RESULT is bot.command-result@1's: ack (the desk did it; DATA is its answer, a page as text and refs, a picture, a receipt), nack (the desk refused; CODE is its fault code and REASON says why), refused (OpenVibe.Bot's gate refused it; CODE is Bot's refusal code) or expired (no answer in time). Every answer also says how the session stands now, so a caller sees it end (idle, ttl, host_lost) without asking again.

data.description: The desk's answer on an ack (bot.command-result@1 data).

run.session-create-request.v1.title: RunSessionCreateRequest
run.session-create-request.v1.description: run.session-create-request@1 (the Desks plan's D6): the body of POST /api/v1/sessions on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.session.create), answered 201 with run.session@1 (state placing). The session is the caller's own: a person's token, or a first-party service acting for a person (X-OV-Subject; the service is recorded as via). MACHINE names one of the person's own machines (an OpenVibe.Bot device they own and let agents use): the session goes there or ends unplaceable, never elsewhere. Without it Run places the desk: on the person's own machines when REQUIREMENTS name user-owned (and only theirs), else on desk hosts that serve other people (first-party, then community, unless REQUIREMENTS narrow it), each of whose desks runs in its own sandbox. Absent REQUIREMENTS mean { kind: run.browser, mobility: session, latency_class: interactive, objective: balanced }. TTL_S (default 3600) and IDLE_S (default 900) bound its life. IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: a repeat from the same person within 24 h with an identical body answers the first session (200); with a different body 409 run.idempotency.conflict.

machine.description: One of the person's own machines, by its OpenVibe.Bot id; the session goes there or nowhere.

run.session.v1.title: RunSession
run.session.v1.description: run.session@1 (the Desks plan's D6): one session on OpenVibe.Run, a browser desk held for one person, as GET /api/v1/sessions/{id} answers it (capability run.session.read) and run.session-list-result@1, POST /api/v1/sessions (run.session.create) and POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/end (run.session.control) carry it. A session is a desk (bot.command@1 kind desk, kind browser) that Run places on a machine and OpenVibe.Bot leases to it (bot.desk-lease@1): on one of the person's own machines where they let agents use it (trust user-owned, never another person's), or on a desk host that serves other people (trust first-party or community: the host's OpenVibe.Node runs every desk in its own sandbox, desk_isolation sandbox, and offers nothing else of the machine). STATES: placing (stored, looking for a machine) -> starting (the desk is leased and starting) -> running (the desk answered) -> ended. An ended session never changes; end.reason says why: ended (POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/end), ttl (ttl_s ran out), idle (no command for idle_s), host_lost (its machine went away or stopped the desk), unplaceable (no machine had room before ttl_s, or none at all) or failed (the desk would not start). USAGE: desk_seconds counts from started_at to ended_at (or now while running), metered to OpenVibe.Billing as one platform.usage-sample@1 per minute (service run, operation browser.desk, unit s, idempotency_key run:<session id>:<minute>). Run mints the id (ses_<ULID>).

owner.description: The person the session is for: only they (or a first-party service acting for them) read, act on or end it.

via.description: The first-party service that asked for the person (service:actor), or null when they asked themselves.

kind.description: A platform.runtime-class@1 name; browser (a headless browser driven over its pipe) is the only kind of session in v1.

ttl_s.description: The most the session lives, from created_at.

idle_s.description: A session no command used this long ends (end.reason idle).

size.description: The desk's page size (bot.command@1 kind desk width and height).

machine.description: The machine (OpenVibe.Bot device) the desk runs on.

desk.description: The desk's name there (bot.command@1 desk), leased to this session alone.

trust.description: The offer's trust class (platform.resource-offer@1): user-owned is always the owner's own machine.

offer_id.description: The platform.resource-offer@1 it was placed on; null when the request named the person's own machine.

reasons.description: Why this machine, in a few words each (the placer's reasons).

started_at.description: When the desk first answered (state running).

desk_seconds.description: Seconds the desk ran (started_at to ended_at, or to now while running); 0 when it never started.

reasons: a shared desk host with room

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
